meta.description: Machine-readable registry of all 52 CMA Part 2 formulas. Cross-referenced against P2002_BLUEPRINT_EXTRACTION.json and P2002_CERTIFICATION_STANDARD.md §D.4/§E.1.

formulas.name: Current Ratio
formulas.notation: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities

variables.name: Current Assets
variables.description: Cash + receivables + inventory + prepaids + marketable securities, expected to convert within 1 year

variables.name: Current Liabilities
variables.description: Obligations due within 1 year (A/P, accrued expenses, short-term debt, current portion of LTD)

commonErrors: Including restricted cash in current assets without verifying liquidity
Misclassifying the current portion of long-term debt as non-current
formulas.examTrap: Candidates often include prepaid expenses as cash equivalents or exclude the current portion of long-term debt from current liabilities.

formulas.name: Quick Ratio (Acid-Test Ratio)
formulas.notation: Quick Ratio = (Cash + Marketable Securities + Accounts Receivable) / Current Liabilities

variables.name: Marketable Securities
variables.description: Short-term investments readily convertible to cash

variables.name: Accounts Receivable
variables.description: Net realizable value of trade receivables

commonErrors: Including inventory in the numerator (excluded in quick ratio)
Including prepaid expenses
formulas.examTrap: The quick ratio excludes inventory because it is the least liquid current asset. Candidates frequently include it, confusing the quick ratio with the current ratio.

formulas.name: Cash Ratio
formulas.notation: Cash Ratio = (Cash + Marketable Securities) / Current Liabilities

variables.name: Marketable Securities
variables.description: Short-term investments readily convertible to cash

commonErrors: Including accounts receivable (AR is excluded from the cash ratio)
Treating restricted cash as unrestricted
formulas.examTrap: The cash ratio is the most conservative liquidity measure. Candidates may apply it where inventory or receivables turn over quickly, making the ratio misleadingly low.

formulas.name: Inventory Turnover
formulas.notation: Inventory Turnover = COGS / Average Inventory

variables.name: Cost of Goods Sold
variables.description: Cost of inventory sold during the period

commonErrors: Using ending inventory instead of average inventory
Using sales instead of COGS
formulas.examTrap: Using sales in the numerator when COGS is required inflates the turnover figure and misrepresents inventory management efficiency.

formulas.name: Days Sales Outstanding (DSO)
formulas.notation: DSO = (Average Accounts Receivable / Net Credit Sales) × 365

variables.name: Net Credit Sales
variables.description: Total credit sales less returns and allowances

commonErrors: Using 360 days instead of 365
Using total sales instead of credit sales
formulas.examTrap: The CMA exam uses 365 days (not 360). A low DSO is generally favorable but may indicate overly restrictive credit policies.

formulas.name: Days Payable Outstanding (DPO)
formulas.notation: DPO = (Average Accounts Payable / Total Purchases) × 365
commonErrors: Using 360 days
Using COGS directly without adjusting for inventory change
formulas.examTrap: Purchases must be computed indirectly if not given: Purchases = COGS + ΔInventory. A high DPO may signal liquidity problems rather than favorable credit terms.

formulas.name: Debt-to-Equity Ratio
formulas.notation: D/E = Total Liabilities / Total Shareholders' Equity

variables.name: Total Shareholders' Equity
variables.description: Common stock + APIC + retained earnings + AOCI − treasury stock

commonErrors: Using only long-term debt instead of total liabilities
Omitting operating lease liabilities (ASC 842)
formulas.examTrap: Know which variant the question asks for—Debt-to-Equity (total liabilities) vs. Long-Term Debt-to-Equity (LT debt only).

formulas.name: Times Interest Earned (Interest Coverage)
formulas.notation: TIE = EBIT / Interest Expense

variables.name: Interest Expense
variables.description: Total interest incurred (including amortization of bond discount/premium)

commonErrors: Using net income instead of EBIT
Using only cash interest paid rather than total interest expense
formulas.examTrap: EBIT is before interest and taxes. Using EBT or net income in the numerator understates the coverage ratio.

formulas.name: Gross Margin Percentage
formulas.notation: Gross Margin % = (Gross Profit / Net Sales) × 100

variables.name: Net Sales
variables.description: Total sales less returns, allowances, and discounts

commonErrors: Using total sales before returns and allowances
Confusing gross margin with markup (markup = GP / COGS)
formulas.examTrap: Gross Margin % = GP / Sales. Markup % = GP / COGS. These are different metrics—candidates frequently confuse them.

formulas.name: Operating Margin Percentage
formulas.notation: Operating Margin % = (Operating Income / Net Sales) × 100

variables.name: Operating Income
variables.description: Gross Profit − Operating Expenses (SG&A, R&D, depreciation)

variables.name: Net Sales
variables.description: Total sales less returns, allowances, and discounts

commonErrors: Including non-operating items (interest, gains/losses) in operating income
formulas.examTrap: Operating income excludes interest and taxes. Including them converts the metric to net margin, not operating margin.

formulas.name: Net Margin Percentage
formulas.notation: Net Margin % = (Net Income / Net Sales) × 100

variables.name: Net Income
variables.description: Revenue − all expenses + gains − losses − taxes

variables.name: Net Sales
variables.description: Total sales less returns, allowances, and discounts

commonErrors: Including discontinued operations that distort the sustainable margin
Using net income attributable to non-controlling interests inconsistently
formulas.examTrap: Net margin includes financing and tax strategy effects. Comparing net margins across companies with different capital structures is misleading.

formulas.name: Return on Assets (ROA)
formulas.notation: ROA = Net Income / Average Total Assets

variables.name: Net Income
variables.description: Bottom-line earnings after all expenses and taxes

commonErrors: Using ending total assets instead of average
Using operating income instead of net income without specification
formulas.examTrap: ROA uses average assets, not end-of-period assets, unless the question explicitly states otherwise.

formulas.name: Return on Equity (ROE)
formulas.notation: ROE = (Net Income − Preferred Dividends) / Average Common Shareholders' Equity
commonErrors: Using ending equity vs. average
Not subtracting preferred dividends for common ROE
formulas.examTrap: If preferred stock exists, net income must be reduced by preferred dividends for common ROE. Using total net income overstates returns to common shareholders.

formulas.name: DuPont Identity (ROE Decomposition)
formulas.notation: ROE = NPM × TAT × EM = (Net Income / Sales) × (Sales / Average Total Assets) × (Average Total Assets / Average Equity)
formulas.rounding: Two decimal places (ROE); four decimal places (components)
commonErrors: Using ending values instead of averages for TAT and EM
Computing components with inconsistent base periods
formulas.authority: DuPont Corporation (1914); financial ratio analysis theory
formulas.examTrap: The three-way DuPont reveals whether ROE is driven by profitability (NPM), efficiency (TAT), or leverage (EM). High ROE from high EM signals financial risk, not operational excellence.

formulas.name: Earnings Per Share (EPS)
formulas.notation: Basic EPS = (Net Income − Preferred Dividends) / Weighted Average Common Shares Outstanding

variables.name: Preferred Dividends
variables.description: Dividends on cumulative preferred stock (declared or not)

variables.name: Weighted Average Shares
variables.description: Shares weighted by time outstanding during the period

commonErrors: Using ending shares instead of weighted average
Not subtracting undeclared cumulative preferred dividends
Not retroactively adjusting for stock splits/dividends
formulas.examTrap: Stock splits and stock dividends are applied retroactively to WASO for all periods presented. Failing to adjust understates prior-period EPS.

formulas.name: Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio
formulas.notation: P/E = Market Price per Share / Earnings per Share

variables.name: Market Price per Share
variables.description: Current trading price of one common share

commonErrors: Using basic EPS when diluted EPS is more conservative
Comparing trailing P/E to forward P/E of another company
formulas.authority: Market-based ratio; financial ratio analysis theory
formulas.examTrap: P/E ratios are not comparable across industries. A 'low' P/E in a cyclical industry may signal peak earnings about to decline, not a bargain.

formulas.name: Dividend Yield
formulas.notation: Dividend Yield = (Annual Dividends per Share / Market Price per Share) × 100

variables.name: Dividends per Share
variables.description: Total annual dividends declared per common share

variables.name: Market Price per Share
variables.description: Current trading price of one common share

commonErrors: Using one quarter's dividend × 4 without confirming representativeness
Using wrong share price date
formulas.authority: Market-based ratio; financial ratio analysis theory
formulas.examTrap: A high dividend yield may result from a declining stock price (denominator falling), not from generous dividends.

formulas.name: Book Value per Share
formulas.notation: BVPS = (Total Shareholders' Equity − Preferred Equity) / Common Shares Outstanding

variables.name: Preferred Equity
variables.description: Liquidation value or par value of preferred stock

variables.name: Common Shares Outstanding
variables.description: Shares issued − treasury shares, at period end

commonErrors: Using average shares instead of period-end shares
Not subtracting preferred equity
formulas.examTrap: Book value reflects historical cost, not market value. A stock trading below BVPS does not necessarily mean undervaluation—assets may be impaired.

formulas.name: Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL)
formulas.notation: DOL = Contribution Margin / Operating Income
commonErrors: Using gross margin instead of contribution margin
Computing at the wrong sales level
formulas.examTrap: DOL is a point elasticity—it changes at different sales levels. DOL of 3 means a 1% sales increase produces a 3% operating income increase at that specific sales level.
formulas.note: Cross-domain alias: identical to DA-05 (Degree of Operating Leverage, CVP form). Retained in both domains for per-domain completeness; case authors may cite either ID.

formulas.name: Degree of Financial Leverage (DFL)
formulas.notation: DFL = EBIT / EBT = Operating Income / (Operating Income − Interest Expense)
commonErrors: Not adjusting denominator for preferred dividends grossed up for taxes
formulas.examTrap: If preferred stock exists, denominator must also subtract Preferred Dividends / (1 − t), reflecting the after-tax nature of preferred dividends.

formulas.name: Sustainable Growth Rate
formulas.notation: SGR = ROE × (1 − Dividend Payout Ratio)
commonErrors: Using dividend yield instead of payout ratio
Assuming constant SGR when ROE fluctuates
formulas.examTrap: SGR assumes constant capital structure, dividend policy, and asset turnover. It is a theoretical maximum, not a forecast.

formulas.name: Dividend Payout Ratio
formulas.notation: Payout Ratio = Dividends per Share / Earnings per Share
commonErrors: Using total dividends instead of per-share values
Confusing payout ratio with retention ratio (b = 1 − payout)
formulas.examTrap: Retention ratio is the complement: b = 1 − Payout Ratio. Sustainable growth (SGR) requires the retention ratio, not the payout ratio directly.

formulas.name: Free Cash Flow (FCF)
formulas.notation: FCF = Operating Cash Flow − Net Capital Expenditures
commonErrors: Including financing or investing inflows
Treating EBITDA as a proxy for FCF
formulas.examTrap: FCF measures discretionary cash available after maintaining the asset base. Common error: adding borrowing proceeds (a financing inflow) into FCF.

formulas.name: Total Asset Turnover
formulas.notation: Total Asset Turnover = Net Sales / Average Total Assets
commonErrors: Using ending assets instead of average
Comparing asset-heavy and asset-light firms without context
formulas.examTrap: A low ratio for a capital-intensive manufacturer is normal; the same ratio for a retailer signals inefficiency. Always interpret within the industry business model.

formulas.name: Debt-to-Assets Ratio
formulas.notation: Debt-to-Assets = Total Liabilities / Total Assets
commonErrors: Using long-term debt only instead of total liabilities
Confusing D/A with D/E
formulas.examTrap: D/A and the equity-financing ratio sum to 1. D/A is the safer metric when equity can approach zero (making D/E explode).

formulas.name: Expected Return (Probability-Weighted)
formulas.notation: E(R) = Σ(P_i × R_i)

variables.name: Probability of State i
variables.description: Likelihood of economic state i occurring (must sum to 1.0)

variables.name: Return in State i
variables.description: Expected return if state i occurs

commonErrors: Probabilities not summing to 1.0
Using simple arithmetic mean instead of probability-weighted average
formulas.examTrap: Expected return is a probability-weighted average, not a simple arithmetic mean. Candidates frequently compute the simple mean of returns without applying probabilities.

formulas.name: Standard Deviation of Returns
formulas.notation: σ = sqrt(Σ(P_i × (R_i − E(R))²))

variables.name: Standard Deviation
variables.description: Measure of total risk (dispersion around expected return)

commonErrors: Computing population standard deviation instead of applying probability weights
Forgetting the square root
formulas.examTrap: Standard deviation measures total risk (systematic + unsystematic). In a diversified portfolio, only systematic risk (beta) matters.

formulas.name: Coefficient of Variation
formulas.notation: CV = σ / E(R)
commonErrors: Reversing numerator and denominator
Using variance instead of standard deviation
formulas.examTrap: CV measures risk per unit of return—the correct metric for comparing investments with different expected returns.

formulas.name: Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM)
formulas.notation: R_e = R_f + β(R_m − R_f)

variables.name: Risk-Free Rate
variables.description: Return on a risk-free asset (typically 10-year U.S. Treasury)

variables.name: Beta
variables.description: Measure of systematic risk relative to the market (β_market = 1)

variables.name: Market Return
variables.description: Expected return on the market portfolio

variables.name: Market Risk Premium
variables.description: Excess return demanded for bearing market risk

commonErrors: Using historical market return instead of expected
Using wrong risk-free rate maturity
Computing beta from non-comparable index
formulas.examTrap: CAPM gives the required return (cost of equity), not the expected return of the stock. Using historical beta without adjustment for mean reversion is a known limitation.

formulas.name: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC)
formulas.notation: WACC = (E/V × R_e) + (P/V × R_p) + (D/V × R_d × (1 − t))
commonErrors: Using pre-tax cost of debt instead of after-tax
Omitting preferred stock component
Using book values instead of market values for weights
formulas.examTrap: Three classic WACC errors: (1) Pre-tax cost of debt—must multiply by (1 − t). (2) Omitting preferred stock entirely. (3) Book value weights instead of market value weights.

formulas.name: Cost of Preferred Stock
formulas.notation: R_p = D_p / P_p

variables.name: Annual Preferred Dividend
variables.description: Stated dollar dividend per preferred share

commonErrors: Subtracting flotation costs from dividend instead of from price
Using par value instead of market price
formulas.examTrap: Preferred dividends are not tax-deductible. Unlike debt, there is no (1 − t) adjustment for preferred stock in WACC.

formulas.name: Cost of Debt (After-Tax)
formulas.notation: After-Tax Cost of Debt = R_d × (1 − t)

variables.name: Pre-Tax Cost of Debt
variables.description: Yield to maturity on the firm's debt

commonErrors: Using coupon rate instead of YTM
Using average tax rate instead of marginal rate
Forgetting (1 − t)
formulas.examTrap: The pre-tax cost of debt for WACC is YTM, not the coupon rate. Using the coupon rate ignores whether the bond trades at a premium or discount.

formulas.name: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)
formulas.notation: EOQ = sqrt(2DS / H)

variables.name: Holding Cost
variables.description: Annual carrying cost per unit (storage, insurance, obsolescence, opportunity cost)

commonErrors: Using demand in dollars vs. units inconsistently
Double-counting or omitting opportunity cost in H
formulas.examTrap: D and H must be in the same time units (both annual). If monthly demand is given, multiply by 12 first. If holding cost is a percentage, multiply by unit cost to get H in dollars.

formulas.name: Forward/FX Premium or Discount
formulas.notation: Forward Premium/Discount (%) = ((Forward Rate − Spot Rate) / Spot Rate) × (360 / Days) × 100

variables.name: Forward Rate
variables.description: Agreed-upon exchange rate for future settlement

variables.name: Spot Rate
variables.description: Current exchange rate for immediate delivery

variables.name: Forward Period
variables.description: Number of days to forward contract maturity

commonErrors: Reversing numerator (S − F) flipping the sign
Using 365 days instead of 360 (FX convention)
formulas.authority: International finance theory; interest rate parity
formulas.examTrap: FX markets use a 360-day year. A positive result means the foreign currency trades at a forward premium (strengthening). Direction matters for interpretation.

formulas.name: Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC)
formulas.notation: CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO
commonErrors: ADDING DPO instead of subtracting it
Using 360 days instead of 365
Using COGS instead of purchases when computing DPO
formulas.examTrap: Lower CCC frees cash. A negative CCC means suppliers finance operations. Compute DPO from purchases (Purchases = COGS + ΔInventory) when purchases are not given.

formulas.name: Cost of Common Equity — Dividend Discount Model (Gordon Growth)
formulas.notation: Re = D1 / P0 + g
commonErrors: Using D0 (last paid dividend) instead of D1
Ignoring flotation costs when valuing NEW equity
formulas.examTrap: D1 = D0 × (1 + g). For NEW common equity, adjust the denominator for flotation costs: Re = D1 / (P0 × (1 − F)) + g. Requires constant perpetual growth; not applicable to non-dividend payers.

formulas.name: Breakeven Point (Units)
formulas.notation: BE_units = Fixed Costs / CM per Unit

variables.name: Fixed Costs
variables.description: Total fixed costs (do not vary with output)

variables.name: Contribution Margin per Unit
variables.description: Selling Price − Variable Cost per Unit

commonErrors: Using selling price instead of contribution margin
Including variable costs in the numerator
Not separating semi-variable (mixed) costs
formulas.examTrap: Semi-variable (mixed) costs must be separated into fixed and variable components before computing breakeven.

formulas.name: Breakeven Point (Dollars)
formulas.notation: BE_$ = Fixed Costs / CM Ratio

variables.name: Contribution Margin Ratio
variables.description: CM per Unit / Selling Price, or Total CM / Total Sales

commonErrors: Using markup percentage instead of CM ratio
Using gross margin ratio instead of CM ratio
formulas.examTrap: CM Ratio = CM / Sales. Gross Margin Ratio = Gross Profit / Sales. These are different—CM excludes all variable costs, not just COGS.

formulas.name: Target Profit (Units)
formulas.notation: Units_target = (Fixed Costs + Target Operating Profit) / CM per Unit
commonErrors: Using after-tax target profit without grossing up for taxes
Forgetting to add fixed costs in numerator
formulas.examTrap: If the question gives target net income (after-tax), convert: Target Pre-Tax = After-Tax Profit / (1 − t). Then add to fixed costs.

formulas.name: Margin of Safety
formulas.notation: MOS (%) = ((Actual Sales − Breakeven Sales) / Actual Sales) × 100
commonErrors: Reversing numerator (BE − Actual) giving negative MOS
Mixing dollar and unit measures
formulas.examTrap: Margin of safety answers 'How much can sales decline before the company incurs a loss?' Always expressed as a percentage of actual sales.

formulas.name: Degree of Operating Leverage (CVP Form)
formulas.notation: DOL = Contribution Margin / Operating Income
commonErrors: Using gross margin instead of CM
Computing at the wrong activity level
formulas.examTrap: DOL is highest near the breakeven point (operating income → 0 in denominator). Very high DOL signals both high upside and high downside risk.
formulas.note: Cross-domain alias: identical to FA-19 (Degree of Operating Leverage). Retained in both domains for per-domain completeness; case authors may cite either ID.

formulas.name: Weighted Average Contribution Margin
formulas.notation: WACM = Σ(Sales Mix_i × CM_i)

variables.name: Sales Mix Percentage of Product i
variables.description: Proportion of total units from product i (must sum to 1.0)

variables.name: CM per Unit of Product i

formulas.rounding: Two decimal places (WACM); four decimal places (mix %)
commonErrors: Using revenue mix instead of unit mix
Mix percentages not summing to 1.0
formulas.authority: Managerial accounting theory; multi-product CVP analysis
formulas.examTrap: Multi-product breakeven yields total units, not per-product units. After computing total breakeven units, multiply by sales mix % to get per-product units.

formulas.name: Shut-Down Point
formulas.notation: Shut Down if: Price < Minimum AVC

variables.name: Minimum Average Variable Cost
variables.description: Lowest point on the AVC curve

commonErrors: Comparing price to average total cost (ATC) instead of AVC
Shutting down when P between AVC and ATC (should continue short-run)
formulas.examTrap: In the short run, continue if P ≥ AVC, even if P < ATC. Continuing covers variable costs and contributes to fixed costs. Shutting down when P ≥ AVC increases losses.

formulas.name: Sell-or-Process-Further Decision
formulas.notation: Process Further if: Incremental Revenue − Incremental Cost > 0

variables.name: Incremental Revenue
variables.description: Revenue after processing − Revenue at split-off

commonErrors: Including allocated joint costs (sunk at split-off—irrelevant)
Comparing total profitability instead of incremental
formulas.authority: IMA SMA on relevant costing; joint product decision theory
formulas.examTrap: Joint costs allocated to products are irrelevant—they are sunk at the split-off point. Only incremental revenues and costs beyond split-off matter.

formulas.name: Transfer Price (Minimum)
formulas.notation: Transfer Price_min = Variable Cost per Unit + Opportunity Cost per Unit

variables.name: Variable Cost
variables.description: Incremental cost of producing one unit

variables.name: Opportunity Cost
variables.description: CM foregone on external sales sacrificed (only when at full capacity)

commonErrors: Forgetting opportunity cost when at full capacity
Using full absorption cost instead of variable cost
formulas.authority: IMA SMA on relevant costing; transfer pricing theory
formulas.examTrap: Idle capacity → OC = $0 → minimum TP = VC. Full capacity → OC = CM lost from displaced external sales. The distinction is critical on the CMA exam.

formulas.name: Expected Value
formulas.notation: EV = Σ(P_i × Outcome_i)

variables.name: Probability of Outcome i
variables.description: Likelihood of outcome i (must sum to 1.0)

commonErrors: Probabilities not summing to 1.0
Confusing expected value with most likely outcome
formulas.examTrap: EV is a long-run average, not a prediction of a single outcome. Higher EV does not guarantee a better result in any given instance.

formulas.name: Value of Perfect Information
formulas.notation: EVPI = EV_with perfect information − EV_without perfect information

variables.name: EV with Perfect Information
variables.description: Weighted average of best outcomes under each state

variables.name: EV without Perfect Information
variables.description: EV of the optimal decision under uncertainty

commonErrors: Computing EV with PI by taking the simple best outcome instead of probability-weighting
Confusing EVPI with maximum possible payoff
formulas.examTrap: EVPI is the maximum a decision-maker should pay for perfect information. If market research costs more than EVPI, don't buy it—regardless of accuracy.

formulas.name: Expected Loss
formulas.notation: Expected Loss = Probability × Impact

variables.name: Impact
variables.description: Financial magnitude if the loss occurs

commonErrors: Using ordinal labels ('likely') without converting to numeric
Using worst-case impact instead of expected impact
formulas.authority: COSO ERM (2017) — Component 3: Performance, Principle 10 (Identifies Risk)
formulas.examTrap: Expected loss is a probability-weighted average, not the worst-case scenario. Risk response should consider both expected loss and tail risk.

formulas.name: Risk Score
formulas.notation: Risk Score = Likelihood × Severity

variables.name: Likelihood
variables.description: Probability or frequency of occurrence on an ordinal scale (e.g., 1–5)

variables.name: Severity
variables.description: Magnitude of impact on an ordinal scale (e.g., 1–5)

commonErrors: Using different scales for L and S (e.g., 1–3 for L, 1–5 for S)
Adding instead of multiplying
formulas.authority: COSO ERM (2017) — Component 3: Performance, Principle 10 (Identifies Risk)
formulas.examTrap: Risk heat maps multiply likelihood × severity, not add them. A risk that is almost certain (5) with moderate impact (3) = 15, not 8. Adding understates high-likelihood, high-severity risks.

formulas.name: Residual Risk
formulas.notation: Residual Risk = Inherent Risk − Controls Mitigation

variables.name: Inherent Risk
variables.description: Risk level before any controls or mitigation

variables.name: Controls Mitigation
variables.description: Risk reduction attributable to internal controls

commonErrors: Reversing direction (Controls − Inherent)
Assuming residual risk reaches zero
formulas.authority: COSO ERM (2017) — Component 3: Performance, Principle 11 (Assesses Severity of Risk, including residual risk)
formulas.examTrap: Residual risk can never be zero—no control system is perfect. The CMA exam expects candidates to recognize that some residual risk always remains.

formulas.name: Net Present Value (NPV)
formulas.notation: NPV = Σ(CF_t / (1 + r)^t) − I_0

variables.name: Cash Flow in Period t
variables.description: Expected net after-tax cash inflow in period t

variables.name: Discount Rate
variables.description: Required rate of return or cost of capital

formulas.rounding: Nearest whole dollar; carry 4 decimal places for discount factors
commonErrors: Wrong discount rate (real vs. nominal, pre-tax vs. after-tax)
Omitting working capital recovery in terminal year
Including sunk costs in cash flows
Double-counting inflation
formulas.authority: Capital budgeting theory (Fisher, 1930); NPV decision rule
formulas.examTrap: NPV uses cash flows, not accounting income. Depreciation is added back via the tax shield. Discount rate must match cash flow type—nominal cash flows need nominal rates.

formulas.name: Profitability Index (PI)
formulas.notation: PI = PV of Future Cash Flows / Initial Investment

variables.name: PV of Future Cash Flows
variables.description: Sum of discounted cash inflows (excluding I_0)

commonErrors: Including I_0 in numerator (gives NPV/I_0 + 1, not PI)
Using undiscounted cash flows
formulas.examTrap: PI is NPV-based (uses discounted cash flows), not simple benefit-cost ratio. PI > 1 means NPV > 0. Correct ranking metric under capital rationing.

formulas.name: Payback Period
formulas.notation: Payback = Initial Investment / Annual Cash Flow (uniform CF); cumulative otherwise
commonErrors: Using accounting income instead of cash flows
Not using cumulative method for non-uniform CFs
formulas.examTrap: Payback ignores the time value of money and cash flows beyond the payback period. It is a liquidity/screening tool, not a profitability measure.

formulas.name: Discounted Payback Period
formulas.notation: DPP = time until cumulative discounted cash flows ≥ I_0
commonErrors: Using undiscounted cash flows (defeats the purpose)
Stopping at the wrong year
formulas.examTrap: Discounted payback corrects for time value of money but still ignores post-cutoff cash flows. It is always longer than simple payback.

formulas.name: Equivalent Annual Annuity (EAA)
formulas.notation: EAA = NPV / PVIFA(r, n) = NPV / ((1 − (1 + r)^(−n)) / r)

variables.name: Net Present Value
variables.description: Sum of discounted net cash flows

commonErrors: Comparing NPVs directly for unequal-life projects
Using wrong annuity factor
formulas.examTrap: When comparing mutually exclusive projects with unequal lives, NPV alone is insufficient. EAA converts lump-sum NPV to an annualized equivalent for apples-to-apples comparison.

formulas.name: After-Tax Cash Flow
formulas.notation: ATCF = (Revenue − Cash Operating Expenses) × (1 − t) + (Depreciation × t)

variables.name: Cash Operating Expenses
variables.description: Variable and fixed cash costs (excludes depreciation)

commonErrors: Omitting the depreciation tax shield (Depr × t)
Treating depreciation as a cash outflow
Using average tax rate instead of marginal
formulas.examTrap: Depreciation is non-cash—it does NOT directly reduce cash flow. It reduces taxable income, creating a tax shield. Only the tax shield (Depreciation × t) is added back.

formulas.name: MACRS Depreciation
formulas.notation: MACRS Depreciation_t = Cost × MACRS Rate_t (from IRS Pub 946 tables)

variables.name: MACRS Rate for Year t
variables.description: Statutory percentage from IRS tables (3-, 5-, 7-year property classes)

commonErrors: Subtracting salvage value before applying MACRS rate (MACRS ignores salvage)
Using wrong recovery period
Wrong half-year convention application in disposal year
formulas.examTrap: MACRS ignores salvage value entirely—depreciable basis = full cost. Half-year convention: only 50% of Year 1 rate in Year 1, remainder in Year n+1. A 3-year property is depreciated over 4 tax years.

formulas.name: Accounting Rate of Return (ARR)
formulas.notation: ARR = Average Annual Net Income / Average Investment

variables.name: Average Annual Net Income
variables.description: Average accrual-basis income over project life (after depreciation and tax)

commonErrors: Using cash flows instead of accounting net income
Using initial investment instead of average investment
formulas.examTrap: ARR is the only capital budgeting method using accounting income rather than cash flows. It ignores the time value of money entirely.

formulas.name: Internal Rate of Return (IRR)
formulas.notation: IRR = discount rate r where NPV = Σ(CF_t / (1 + r)^t) − I_0 = 0; accept if IRR > required return (WACC)
commonErrors: Accepting projects whose IRR is below WACC
Ranking mutually exclusive projects of different scale or timing by IRR
Ignoring the multiple-IRR problem when cash flows change sign more than once
formulas.authority: Capital budgeting theory (Fisher, 1930); IRR decision rule
formulas.examTrap: IRR has no closed form — it is found by interpolation or calculator. The IRR method assumes reinvestment at the IRR itself; NPV assumes reinvestment at WACC. For independent projects IRR and NPV agree; for mutually exclusive projects they can conflict.

F.name: Professional Ethics
F.note: Domain F tests the IMA Statement of Ethical Professional Practice, SOX 2002, FCPA, and corporate governance. All items are conceptual—no quantitative formulas are tested.
